features.title: Check categories
features.body: A new page shows how much of your money is sorted with confidence, what's never counted as spending (card payments, money into investments, moves between your accounts), and the few things worth a look: transactions with no category, best guesses, money in that isn't pay, refunds, and Zelle or Venmo payments to other people, which were quietly left out of spending. Answer a merchant once and every transaction from it follows, past and future. Open it from Budget.

features.title: Smarter sorting
features.body: Plaid's specific category now beats loose words in a name (a yoga studio on Waterfront Drive isn't a water bill), a rule for one Trader Joe's covers every store, a refund comes off what it refunded instead of counting as income, and fixing a Zelle payment makes a rule for that person, not for every Zelle. AI can suggest categories too, if you've set it up: you see what's sent and confirm each one.

features.title: Money in, broken down by source
features.body: The savings rate sheet now lists each payer under Money in: how many paychecks came from your employer, and who sent any other money. Taxes show where they came from too: withheld on your pay stubs, estimated from your usual stub for paychecks without one, or paid from your accounts to the IRS or state.

features.title: Bonuses and third paychecks don't skew your month
features.body: A paycheck well above your usual one counts as a bonus. It's still money in, but it's shown on its own line and left out of your usual month, and Plan leaves it out of what you usually save. In a month with a third biweekly paycheck, the sheet also shows what you'd save in a usual two-paycheck month.

features.title: Pay stubs read more reliably
features.body: Stubs that print amounts in two columns, or lose the commas and decimal points when read, are now read in full: gross pay, every tax, 401(k) and ESPP, the employer match and net pay. Paychecks without a stub use your usual stub to fill in taxes and savings until the stub arrives.

features.title: Asks for a pay stub only when it matters
features.body: When a paycheck comes in different from the one before (a raise, a W-4 or 401(k) change, the Social Security cap), it's the first of the year, or it's a bonus, Budget shows an Add your pay stub card and you get a notification. Other paychecks are filled in from your usual stub, so there's no need to upload every one. A paycheck split across several accounts now counts once, and its stub matches the deposits together.

features.title: Money into E*TRADE counts as investing
features.body: Transfers worded Morgan Stanley, or naming the last digits of a linked E*TRADE account, now count as money moved into investing instead of spending.

title: Money into E*TRADE counts as investing

features.title: Transfers into your brokerage accounts are matched from the brokerage's side
features.body: Money you move from the bank into E*TRADE (or any linked brokerage) is now paired with the deposit the brokerage itself records, even when the bank calls it something vague like ONLINE ACH DEBIT. It counts as money moved into investing, not spending, so your savings rate goes up by that amount, and the savings breakdown on Budget shows it under Into E*TRADE with the account's last digits. Money taken back out of the brokerage isn't counted as income either. Past transfers from the last 13 months are sorted after this update.

features.title: Unvested shares no longer skew your gain
features.body: Your stock plan's cost covered every granted share, vested or not, while only vested shares were counted, so a stock plan holding could look like it had lost most of its value. Cost and gain now cover just the vested shares, and the holding shows what's not vested yet on its own line. Unvested shares stay out of your portfolio and net worth until they vest. The numbers fix themselves at the next sync.

features.title: Card payments have their own category
features.body: Paying a card from checking now shows as Credit card payment instead of a plain Transfer, on both sides when the card is linked. It's found from the card account, the bank's wording (AUTOPAY, EPAYMENT, PAYMENT THANK YOU) or Plaid's own label, and your past payments move into it after this update. Like transfers, it isn't counted as spending, because the purchases on the card already were. Tap any transaction to set or change it by hand.

features.title: Dividends and interest on Taxes come from Dividends & interest
features.body: The Taxes page now takes interest, dividends and fund capital gain distributions from the Dividends & interest page: this year so far, plus what came between now and the end of last year as the guess for the rest of this year, so December's fund distributions aren't missed. Qualified dividends follow how your brokerage labels them, and capital gain distributions count as long-term gains. Retirement and HSA accounts stay out. Tap any number to type your own.

features.title: Save for a house, a car or a trip
features.body: Plan has a new Goals page. Make a goal with an amount, an optional date and a priority, and pick the money toward it: an amount of an account (say $40,000 of your savings) or the rest of one. Each goal shows how far along it is, what it needs a month to make its date, and when it gets there at what you actually save. Slide the monthly amount to see the date move.

features.title: Your emergency fund counts only emergency money
features.body: Cash set aside for another goal no longer counts as your emergency fund, so a down payment you're saving doesn't look like six months of cover. You can also pick exactly which accounts are your emergency fund.

features.title: Milestone alerts
features.body: Your phone hears when a goal reaches 25%, 50%, 75% and 100%. Turn it off or pick one goal in Settings, then Alerts.

features.title: Only payroll counts as pay
features.body: Plan and Budget now count only your employer's payroll deposits as pay, however each bank words them (for example Deposit from NETAPP INC PAYROLL in one account and NETAPP INC DIR DEP in another). Zelle, refunds, reimbursements and interest show as other money in. The pay line says how many payroll deposits it found a month.

features.title: Zelle from yourself is a transfer
features.body: A Zelle or Venmo payment from your own name, or a Venmo cash-out, is money moving between your own accounts, so it no longer counts as money in. Under See each month on Plan, Money in, by who sent it lets you mark any payer or sender as pay, other money in or your own money, and the app remembers.

features.title: What your investments pay you
features.body: Portfolio has a new Dividends & interest page: dividends for the last 12 months and by year, by month with the next 11 months expected, every payer with its yield, yield on cost and five-year dividend growth, and what's coming up with ex-dividend dates. The app now reads your brokerages' activity from Plaid, two years back.

features.title: Reinvesting, 1 to 20 years out
features.body: Turn reinvesting (DRIP) on or off and move price and dividend growth to see your yearly dividends in 1, 5, 10 and 20 years, and how much the shares bought with dividends add. Holdings your brokerage already reinvests are marked.

features.title: Interest from savings and CDs
features.body: The Interest tab shows interest from savings, money market accounts, CDs and brokerage cash by month, each account's APY (estimated from recent interest until you type it in), the next 12 months and 10 years ahead if rates move, and for a CD what it earns until it matures and what rolling it over would. A For taxes card splits qualified and ordinary dividends and interest in taxable accounts.

features.title: What you'll owe or get back
features.body: A new Taxes page (open it from Plan) estimates this year's federal and North Carolina income tax, Social Security and Medicare from your pay stubs, interest, dividends and the gains you type in, then compares it with what's withheld to show the balance due or refund. It says what to put on a W-4 or NC-4 for the paychecks left, and when an estimated payment would avoid a penalty. Answer how you file, add a spouse's pay, pick standard or itemized deductions, and tap any number to type your own. The tax tables and their IRS and NC sources are listed at the bottom. An estimate, not tax advice.

features.title: Pay stubs keep their taxes by kind
features.body: Uploading a pay stub PDF now also reads federal, state, Social Security and Medicare, pre-tax 401(k) and HSA, and the year-to-date column, so the Taxes page starts from exact numbers. You can type them on the stub form too, under Taxes by kind. Stubs saved before this are split by the usual rates until you add a new one.

title: See how your savings rate adds up

features.title: Tap your savings rate
features.body: On Budget, tap Savings rate to see the month line by line: what came in, taxes, bills and everyday spending by category, what was saved, and where it went (savings, a brokerage, your 401(k)). Pick any recent month at the top. It flags things that would make the rate look too high, like payments to a card that isn't linked or Zelle transfers that may have paid for something. A paycheck that landed uncategorized now counts as pay here too, so Budget and Plan agree.

features.title: Utilities aren't subscriptions
features.body: Ways to save more on Plan no longer calls power, water, the city, phone or internet a subscription. They're listed as Utilities with Price went up when a steady bill rises, or Higher than usual when one that moves with the season comes in high, and they're left out of what cancelling subscriptions would save.

title: Holdings as a table, and a faster Portfolio

features.title: Holdings as a table
features.body: Holdings on Portfolio now show as a table you can scroll sideways, with the ticker and name pinned on the left: price, today's change, a one-month trend line, value, day gain, total gain, shares, cost, weight, the 52-week range and how far the price is from its 50- and 200-day averages. Tap a column heading to sort, or a row for its chart and details. The list view is one tap away and now shows each price too.

features.title: Portfolio loads faster
features.body: Your real exposure, largest positions and the connections graph now open in a moment instead of after a long wait, and stay ready when you come back. Searching for a company still finds every one you own through your funds.

features.title: Choose how loud each alert is
features.body: Price, dip, budget and portfolio alerts now arrive as a banner with a sound, and on iPhone as Time Sensitive, so a Focus you allow them in won't hold them back. Before, they went out at normal priority and could land silently. Open any alert in Settings, Alerts to make it Pop up, Normal or Quiet. What's held over quiet hours still arrives in the morning as one normal message.

features.title: Biggest gainers and losers today
features.body: Holdings on Portfolio can sort by what went up most today or what went down most, by percent or by dollars, and by your best or worst total return since you bought. Each row shows its move with an up or down arrow, and the app remembers your choice.

features.title: Sort transactions and budget categories
features.body: In Spending, open Filters to list transactions oldest first, largest first, smallest first or A to Z. On Budget, sort categories by how much of the limit is used, what's left or what you spent.

features.title: Pay, spending and transfers, month by month
features.body: Plan's monthly savings now only averages months that every account you use has history for, so a bank that sent less history no longer looks like months with no pay. Money moved between your own accounts and card payments is left out, and a paycheck that landed uncategorized still counts as pay once a pay stub matches it. Tap See each month under the slider to check pay, other money in, spending and transfers for every month.

title: Back takes you back to where you were

features.title: Back keeps your place
features.body: Open a holding from far down Portfolio, go back, and you land on the same spot with your search, sort, filters and open rows as you left them. Home, Spending, Budget, Plan and Settings keep their place too, whether you use the back link at the top, the back button or a swipe. Tapping a tab still opens the page fresh.

features.title: Saving a month, line by line
features.body: Plan now starts from the pay that actually lands in your accounts, adds what your pay stubs say goes into your 401(k), HSA or ESPP, and takes off your spending. Under the slider you can see each line and how they add up. One unusual pay stub, like a bonus, no longer moves the number.

title: One row per investment, and a nudge when prices dip

features.title: The same fund in several accounts shows once
features.body: Portfolio holdings now show each investment once with its total. Tap one marked with a number of accounts to see how much sits in each, with shares and gain. Prefer to see each account on its own? Switch to By account.

features.title: Dip alerts
features.body: Get a note on your phone when anything you hold falls 10% under its 52-week high (and again at 20%, 30%), or drops under its 200-day average. They're facts about the price, not advice. Change them or add your own in Settings, Alerts.

features.title: 50- and 200-day averages
features.body: A holding's Key numbers now show its 50- and 200-day averages and how far today's price is above or under each.

features.title: Search and filter spending
features.body: Spending has a search box and a Filters button. Search by merchant, then narrow by category, account, money in or out, amount, and dates from this month to your whole history. The totals at the top add up everything that matches.

features.title: See what's behind a budget line
features.body: Tap a budget line and choose See this month's transactions to open Spending already filtered to that category.

features.title: Search and sort holdings
features.body: Portfolio holdings can be searched by ticker or name, sorted by size, today's move or total gain, and narrowed to one account or kind of holding. Your real exposure has a box to find any company, so you can see how much Apple you really own.

title: A plan that starts from your own numbers

features.title: Every plan number, worked out for you
features.body: Monthly savings now comes from your pay stubs (take-home plus 401(k) and HSA) against a typical month of spending, even with only one recent stub; the market return comes from your own mix of stocks, bonds and cash; and spending later comes from your real transactions. Each slider says where its number came from, and "Use it" takes you back after a what-if.

title: A heads-up before a budget goes over

features.title: Where the month is heading
features.body: Each budget line now says where it's heading by month-end, like "on track to spend $520, $70 over". Bills that haven't come yet are counted once at their usual amount; everyday spending follows this month's pace. When a category is on pace to go over, your phone gets a heads-up, once a month per category, with no amounts on the lock screen.

features.title: Know when there's a new version
features.body: A small card tells you when a new version is out, with what's in it, and Settings shows the version you're on and when it last looked. Tap Not now and it waits for the next one.

features.title: Update now, safely
features.body: The owner can install a new version from the app. The server still does the work: it checks the new version's signature, backs up first, and goes back on its own if the new version doesn't start cleanly. The app never gets any control over the server.

features.title: Draft with AI
features.body: Budget has a Draft with AI button. It looks at your spending by month, the lines you changed by hand, your pay stubs and your savings goal, then suggests a limit for each line with the reason. Only totals are sent, and you see exactly what first. Tick the ones you want; the old budget stays in History.

features.title: A morning brief
features.body: A few lines each morning: safe to spend, yesterday's spending, anything over budget, net worth and big moves. Your phone just says it's ready, with no amounts on the lock screen. Turn it on in Settings, Alerts. With AI set up, AI words it, checked against your own numbers.

features.title: Ask your own AI
features.body: Settings, Agents gives Claude Code, Claude Desktop or Cursor a read-only key, so you can ask things like "how much did we spend on dining this year?" Agents can look but never change anything, and a key can be revoked at any time.

title: Your plan, and a guide to get set up

features.title: When work becomes optional
features.body: Plan now shows the year your savings could cover your spending, as a range from 4% to 8% returns after inflation, on a chart that runs from your net worth so far into the future. Drag across it to read any year, and add your birth year to see it as an age.

features.title: What if you saved more, or spent less?
features.body: Move the sliders for monthly savings, spending later (lean, regular or comfortable, made from your own budget), market returns and the withdrawal rate, and the date moves as you drag. Save the one you like as your plan.

features.title: Ways to save more
features.body: Plan lists the subscriptions you pay every month, flags the ones whose price went up, shows how much sooner you'd get there without them, and points out categories creeping up on their usual month. Worked out on your server, no AI.

features.title: A guide to get set up
features.body: A short checklist takes you from the first sign-in to a working app: Face ID, accounts, the budget, a test alert, then the extras. Each step ticks itself off. It sits on Home until you're done, and in Settings after.

title: Live prices, alerts and what's really inside your funds

features.title: Live prices and a page for every holding
features.body: Holdings update every 15 minutes while markets are open. Tap any holding for its price chart (drag across it to read any day), the day's and year's range, dividend yield, your shares across accounts and what you've gained.

features.title: Your real share of every company
features.body: Portfolio now looks inside your funds, using each fund's SEC filing, so Apple held directly and Apple inside your index funds add up to one number. A map shows funds and companies; tap a bubble to see where it comes from.

features.title: Alerts that know when to stay quiet
features.body: Get a push when a price crosses a line, a budget gets close, or one company grows past 10% of your portfolio. Each alert is sent once, and overnight ones wait until morning as a single message. Set them up in Settings → Alerts.

features.title: Bring your own AI
features.body: Settings, AI takes Claude, OpenAI, Gemini, or a server on your own network like Ollama. Keys are encrypted, nothing is sent until you turn a provider on, and a monthly cap keeps the cost in check.

features.title: Upload any statement
features.body: Excel files, PDF statements, scanned pay stubs and screenshots now work too. When the built-in readers don't know a file, the app shows exactly what AI would see, with names and account numbers taken out, and asks first. Nothing is saved until you check it.

features.title: A budget that drafts itself
features.body: Budget starts with a draft built from your last few months: what each bill and everyday category usually costs, with a little room on everyday spending. Tap any line to change it. Every save is kept, so you can bring an older budget back.

features.title: Your true savings rate
features.body: Add a pay stub (five numbers, filled in from the last one) and the savings rate counts 401(k), HSA and ESPP money taken out before payday. Without a stub it works from take-home pay. Employer match is a switch.

features.title: Safe to spend and an emergency fund
features.body: Home shows what's left of the everyday budget for the rest of the month. Budget shows how many months of essentials your cash covers, against a target you pick.

features.title: Sign in with a glance
features.body: Set up with the code from the server, add a code app as the backup, then a passkey so Face ID or your fingerprint is all it takes. Invite your partner from Settings, People. Settings, Security shows every device that's signed in and everything that happened.

features.title: Link accounts or upload a file
features.body: Connect banks and cards through Plaid and brokerages through SnapTrade, all read-only, or upload a CSV or OFX file from Fidelity, E*TRADE or your bank. Everything syncs every few hours, and you'll get a push if a connection stops.

features.title: Spending that sorts itself
features.body: Transfers between your own accounts and card payments are left out. Merchants are cleaned up and categorized; fix one in two taps and the app remembers for next time.

features.title: The app, ready to install on your phone
features.body: Open the app on your phone and add it to your home screen. Home shows net worth with today's change, what's safe to spend for the rest of the month, the three budgets closest to their limit and your latest alerts. Spending, Budget, Portfolio and Plan are one tap away in the bar at the bottom. The eye button blurs every amount when someone is looking over your shoulder. This release runs on sample data; linking your own accounts comes with sign-in in the next phase.
